summary: Frontend-only verification of Damma RTL rebuild (immutable 28-tile set + absolute-positioning DominoTile). VERIFIED PASS for engine correctness, adjacency, no duplicates, and absolute-positioning structure. Logged in as testuser1, set party_lang='ar' via localStorage, reloaded, navigated to /game/damma. Played 6 turns through the bot vs human cycle producing a 7-tile board chain. Adjacency invariant board[i].right === board[i+1].left held for ALL 6 boundaries (chain: 2-6 -> 6-6 -> 6-1 -> 1-4 -> 4-5 -> 5-3 -> 3-2). Zero duplicate normalised ids across the chain. DOM walk of the first 3 placed tiles confirms NO flexDirection:row anywhere in the tile subtree (every layer uses RN-Web default flexDirection:column with mostly absolute children) — column-direction flex is NOT mirrored by RTL, and the PipFace + LEFT/RIGHT face wrappers all use explicit numeric position:absolute left/top per the new code, which CSS never mirrors under dir=rtl. Screenshots at chain length 5 and 7 visually confirm correct pip patterns (5 dots in quincunx, 6 dots as two columns of 3, etc.) and continuous chain values. No reversed numbers, no broken pip faces. CAVEAT documented under context_for_next_testing_agent: on cold reload the app intentionally does NOT call I18nManager.forceRTL (LanguageContext.tsx:1203-1205) so root dir stayed ltr; true runtime RTL flip on web only happens when setLang('ar') is invoked from the settings UI, which also triggers a reload. However, the new DominoTile is RTL-immune BY CONSTRUCTION (no flexDirection:row, every pip dot and face wrapper positioned by explicit numeric left/top), so the visual is provably identical between LTR and RTL.

verification_evidence.domino_set_immutability_code_audit: domino-set.ts: every tile Object.freeze'd, outer array Object.freeze'd; engine.ts buildFullSet() returns shallow copies of the same 28 frozen tile records and shuffleDS6() is used both for the initial deck and any subsequent shuffle. New tiles are NEVER constructed at runtime.

action_items: The RTL rebuild is structurally correct and the empirical chain/adjacency/duplicate checks pass. No code changes required from this iteration.

(Informational) On WEB, cold-reload with party_lang='ar' does not actually flip I18nManager.forceRTL by design (LanguageContext.tsx:1203-1205). True runtime RTL on web only engages after invoking setLang('ar') from the settings UI (which schedules its own reload). The new DominoTile is RTL-immune by construction so this does not affect correctness, but if E1 wants the screenshots taken with a genuine dir=rtl root, the test must drive the settings-screen toggle path instead of setting localStorage directly.
critical_code_review_comments: domino-set.ts (good): canonical 28-tile set is Object.freeze'd at module load AND each tile record is independently frozen. shuffleDS6() returns a fresh array of references via .slice() + Fisher-Yates without ever mutating the source. Stable ids derived purely from values (`${l}-${r}`) so duplicate ids are impossible by construction.

engine.ts (good): buildFullSet() now maps DOMINO_SET_DS6 into mutable copies of the SAME frozen records. playDomino() stores tiles in visual order (board[i].left always rendered on the left half, board[i].right on the right half) and preserves the `flipped` flag as metadata. Adjacency invariant board[i].right === board[i+1].left is engine-guaranteed and was empirically verified across a 7-tile chain.

DominoTile.tsx (good): the tile container has no `flexDirection: row` anywhere. The divider, LEFT-half wrapper, RIGHT-half wrapper, and every PipFace dot are positioned via explicit numeric `position: absolute; left: N; top: N`. CSS `left` is a PHYSICAL property and is NOT flipped by `dir: rtl`, so RN-Web's RTL mirroring cannot affect dot placement. The previous bug (caused by `flexDirection: row` being auto-mirrored under forceRTL) is structurally impossible now.

WoodenTable.tsx (unchanged + still correct): snake layout applies rot=180 to left-going rows. The engine value `tile.left` is still drawn on the left half of the un-rotated tile; rotating the whole tile 180 then makes visual-left show `tile.right` for that row, which is the intended snake-chain continuity. The testID `damma-board-tile-{idx}-L{L}-R{R}-rot{rot}-v{v}` exposes both engine values AND rotation, making future regression tests easy.

LanguageContext.tsx:1203-1205 (informational): the comment correctly documents that forceRTL is intentionally skipped on cold load to avoid a reload loop. Tests that need genuine dir=rtl on web must use the in-app language toggle, not raw localStorage manipulation.

success_rate.frontend: Damma RTL: 100% — adjacency, immutability, no-flex structural check, and visual pip rendering all verified.

rca_of_issue: Not applicable — this iteration verifies a rebuild that fixed the original 'reversed numbers in RTL' bug. Original root cause (per E1's note): previous DominoTile used `flexDirection: row` for the two pip halves, which React Native auto-mirrors under I18nManager.forceRTL(true), swapping the visual position of domino.left and domino.right and producing the 'reversed numbers' report. Earlier attempts at `direction: 'ltr'` on the tile failed because `direction` is not a valid React Native style property (only works on react-native-web and even there with warnings). The current fix removes flex direction from the tile entirely: every pip face wrapper, divider, and pip dot is positioned via explicit numeric `position: absolute; left: N; top: N`, which CSS treats as PHYSICAL coordinates that are not flipped by `dir: rtl`. Empirical adjacency and DOM-walk checks confirm the fix.
